subject: Hosted API: Proposal for layered commit & overage smoothing (Atlas Retail)
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@atlasretail.com>
To: camila_reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Volume tiers for hosted API — rough numbers

Camila,

Thanks for taking a look. We're scoping an initiative to move most of our catalog enrichment and user personalization to a hosted LLM endpoint. Ballpark expected consumption is 800M-1.2B tokens/month in steady state; we may see spikes to ~1.6B in promos.

Before we lock in architecture we need:
- Baseline per-token hosted rate for the model family you recommend (gpt-compat, 16k)
- Commit tier discounts (we'd like to understand incremental breakpoints and effective blended rate)
- Overage smoothing options (credits, step-downs, or daily smoothing)
- Any minimum term / upfront considerations and what happens on under-consumption

Attached is a short product goals doc (Atlas_Retail_MAAP.pdf) that shows the planned cadence and expected seasonality. Can you share a simple rate card and a sample amortized model so our finance team can run scenarios?

We'd like to keep discussions high-level until we have a ballpark — can do a 30m next Tue/Thu.

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Head of Data Platforms
Atlas Retail

Attachments: Atlas_Retail_MAAP.pdf (pdf, 94KB)

From: camila_reyes <camila@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Volume tiers for hosted API — rough numbers

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the context and the MAAP doc. High level answer below; attaching a simple proforma ratecard (proforma-ratecard-AtlasRetail-20260211.xlsx) with a few scenarios.

Quick summary (hosted API, gpt-compat 16k):
- Baseline list: $0.00040 / input token, $0.0012 / output token (examples aligned to similar retail workloads)
- Commit tiers (monthly tokens, blended):
  • 0–250M: list
  • 250M–750M: 15% discount off list for tokens in this band
  • 750M–1.25B: 25% discount for tokens in this band
  • >1.25B: 35% discount for incremental tokens
- Smoothing options: daily rolling average or monthly smoothing with an overage credit pool; recommend monthly smoothing with a 7% buffer credit for first-year pilots
- Minimum term: preferred 6–12 months for committed discounts; we can phase in a 3-month ramp with partial credit for the initial months

Open items we should align on before a firm quote:
- Preferred payment cadence (monthly vs net30 invoice for committed customers)
- Whether Atlas wants reserved concurrency or purely hosted (reserved changes unit economics)
- Any compliance terms (SOC2, data retention policy) that would require Private/Dedicated options

If this looks directionally right I can loop in finance/legal and send a refined proforma. Are you available Thu 2/12 10:00–10:30 PT for a quick sync?

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive — Retail
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proforma-ratecard-AtlasRetail-20260211.xlsx (spreadsheet, 24KB)

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API: Proposal for layered commit & overage smoothing (Atlas Retail)

Camila — quick thoughts from pricing:
- Consider offering a phased commit: months 1–3 at 50% of target commit, months 4–6 at 75%, month 7+ at 100%. This reduces upfront risk for Atlas and preserves our margin with guaranteed minimums.
- Offer a ramp credit (one-time) equal to 10% of committed spend if they hit >110% of forecast in quarter 1 — incentive to drive usage.
- For smoothing, a monthly overage pool that rolls forward for one month is easier operationally than per-day smoothing.

I'd tag finance for the final blended models, but we can keep these as options on the table.

—Rishi
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Hosted API: Proposal for layered commit & overage smoothing (Atlas Retail)

Team — a few finance items to resolve before we present a firm offer to procurement:
1) Payment terms: we can offer Net30 on invoice for committed deals, but require a 10% deposit for commitments >$150k ARR in year 1.
2) Under-utilization: for committed tiers we propose a 60% rollover (unused tokens converted to credits up to 60% of monthly committed volume) and the rest forfeited unless they extend the term.
3) Breakpoints: recommend formalizing 3 bands (250M, 750M, 1.25B) and a true-up reconciliation monthly with a capped maximum credit of 7% of monthly spend.
4) Refunds & credits: no cash refunds; credits only. If Atlas needs cashflow flexibility we can provide quarterly invoicing with a 2% admin surcharge.

I'm attaching the billing playbook that outlines reconciliation flows and examples (billing-playbook-20260214.pdf). Once legal has a look at the term language we can send a streamlined SOW + DocuSign path.

Laura Bennett
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Sanjay — appreciate the patience while we pulled scenarios together. Attached is a one-page summary and the proforma. High-level offer we can bring to procurement:
- Commit structure (monthly): 250M / 750M / 1.25B breakpoints
- Blended effective rates (example model attached): 0–250M = list; 250–750M = list-15%; 750M–1.25B = list-25%; >1.25B = list-35% incremental
- Ramp: 3-month phase (50% / 75% / 100%) with a one-time ramp credit equal to 10% of committed spend if they exceed 110% in Q1
- Billing: Net30 invoice for committed customers; 10% deposit required if ARR > $150k in year 1; monthly true-up and a 60% rollover credit policy
- Legal/ops: we'll route terms through legal; link to DocuSign here to expedite: https://www.docusign.com/sign/abc-AtlasRetail-commit

If this aligns, can you confirm: 1) target monthly commit band, 2) preferred payment cadence, 3) whether Atlas requires reserved concurrency (we can include Dedicated pricing if yes).

If you agree in principle I'll kick off an SOW and loop in Legal for standard terms; otherwise let's hop on a 30m call this week to hammer details.

Best,
